stem:
Sana joins an LED to a 1.5 V cell with alligator clips. The LED has a longer pin and a shorter pin.

Answer both parts.

parts.text: Which connection makes the LED glow?

options.text: Longer pin to the cell positive terminal; shorter pin to the cell negative terminal.
Longer pin to the cell negative terminal; shorter pin to the cell positive terminal.
Either way round, because an LED glows in both directions.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: An LED allows current in one direction only, so it glows when the longer pin joins the cell positive terminal and the shorter pin joins the negative terminal.

teacher.key_rationale: LED polarity: longer pin to +, shorter to −. Reversed wiring stays off; LEDs do not glow both ways.
